properties.description:
⭐ THE DECISION THAT CAUSED IT WAS SOUND ON ITS OWN TERMS AND IS NOT THE CAUSE. `fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice` measured a flat 2× on every reply: `detect_gaps` at 157,785 bytes on the wire, refused by a harness; 26,096 after the fix, a 6× improvement with the payload unchanged. **Reverting to always-duplicate resurrects the refusals.** Any remedy must keep that win.

═══ CAUSE 1: THE PREMISE WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE WRONG POPULATION ═══

The recorded reasoning is explicit: gating on the negotiated protocol version was rejected as *'a large invasive change to protect a client nobody could name'*. The check was real and is written down — all three in-repo Python clients read `structuredContent` first, the `j!` test macro reads it only, `proxy.rs` parses neither field. **Every client checked was Anthony's own.** `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` says the field is the point; the verification covered the self-host and not the field. Five days later the field named a client.

⚠️ This is the same shape as `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data-...` and the seam-altitude misreading, both found 2026-08-27: **a measurement whose population did not cover the claim it was used to support.** Third instance in six days.

═══ ⭐⭐ CAUSE 2, AND IT IS THE DEEPER ONE: THE MITIGATION ADDRESSES A PARTY THAT IS NOT IN THE ROOM ═══

The signpost was chosen over an empty `content` block deliberately and for a good reason — silence is indistinguishable from reflow2 not being configured (`req:never-silently-absent`). But read its text: *'**your client** is reading `content` for a tool that declares structured output: read `structuredContent` instead.'*

**It instructs the CLIENT. It is delivered to the AGENT.** The agent cannot change its harness, so the signpost converts silence into an instruction its reader has no power to execute. The recorded claim that the signpost *'protects them anyway'* is therefore false for exactly the population it was written for. The reporter did the only thing left — export to a file and parse it with Python — and named it correctly: *'a post-hoc check, not a read. It cannot replace `search_design` before a create, or `loop_status` before finishing.'*

═══ CAUSE 3: A SPEC `SHOULD` IS BEING DECLINED, WHICH IS LEGAL AND SHIFTS THE BURDEN ═══

MCP 2025-06-18, verified against the specification 2026-08-28, states: *'For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.'* The spec's own worked example carries both. reflow2 declines that SHOULD. A SHOULD may be declined — but declining it moves the entire burden onto clients, and MCP still negotiates `2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26`, which predate the field entirely.

═══ ⚠️ THE COST ESTIMATE THAT DECIDED IT DESERVES RE-MEASURING, AND THIS IS A CANDIDATE NOT A CONCLUSION ═══

The rejection priced version-gating at threading `RequestContext` through 155 handlers and 151 `ok_json` call sites. Two things now bear on that and NEITHER HAS BEEN TESTED: (1) the version machinery ALREADY EXISTS and is tested — `version_is_per_request` and `identity_is_per_request`, with the note that an absent version 'falls back to the peer info recorded at `initialize`'; (2) `json_result` is a SINGLE CHOKE POINT, and making a single choke point carry new state is exactly how read-only shipped on 2026-08-26 — `write_lock` became fallible and the compiler turned all 98 write sites into errors until each was handled, finding a second assembly point review would have missed. **Whether the negotiated version can be captured once at initialize and read at `json_result` has NOT been checked**, and the ~300-line figure predates anyone asking.

═══ WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══

- **One client, one report.** How many other field clients read only `content` is unknown and unmeasured. n=1 for the affected population, exactly as the original premise was n=0.
- **No remedy is asserted.** Options are open in `dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer`.
- **The reporter was unsure of the classification too**, and said so: *'whether this is a reflow2 contract change the TUI has not implemented, or a regression that dropped a fallback.'* It is the former, deliberately — which does not make the outage less real.
properties.name: ROOT CAUSE of the structured-content outage: the premise was 'a client nobody could name' and one is now named — and the mitigation instructs the CLIENT while being read by the AGENT, which cannot change its harness
properties.statement: FIELD REPORT 2026-08-27 (Grok Build TUI, macOS, reflow2 0.39.0), verified against 0.41.0 source 2026-08-28 — STILL TRUE. On a client that forwards only `content`, ~26 named reflow2 tools return the STRUCTURED_ONLY stub and nothing else: get_node, search_design, scan_nodes, loop_status, detect_gaps, export_graph, every constructor. The reporter's words: 'the capture → detect → ask loop is unreadable in this harness. The agent cannot confirm a write, cannot map the user's words to node ids without guessing, and cannot see whether anything is owed.' Refusals and prose tools still work, so the server is reachable and only its ANSWERS are gone.
